In this case, we have to use the identity  $1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ Substituting this into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡x+1}{{sec}^{3}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡x}{{sec}^{3}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡0 \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-0 \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
